scenes.title: 08-r2
lines: An arrow perpendicular to the sheet is a normal. Here we use a unit normal with length one. Draw another unit arrow from the surface toward the light. Parallel arrows mean the sheet faces the light directly, and a wider angle means more oblique illumination. The incoming ray travels opposite to the direction from the surface toward the light.

scenes.title: 08-r3
lines: The dot product measures how aligned two directions are. For two unit arrows it equals the cosine of their angle. Zero degrees gives one, sixty gives one half, and ninety gives zero. Under otherwise equal conditions this is the directional factor for diffuse direct light. Light intensity and material must also be included to obtain the final displayed brightness.

scenes.title: 08-r6
lines: Let us calculate just the red color channel. Set the stored values to point eight, point two and point one. With the normal equal to the first basis direction, weights are one, zero and zero, giving point eight. Rotate thirty degrees toward the second basis direction and the weights become approximately point eight six six, point five and zero. Only the normal changed; the stored values stayed fixed.
